correctness.rationale: For all prime powers and all n,r,s,t in their stated ranges, the commuting projection decomposition gives a transitive GL_n orbit with stabilizer four GL factors. Independent direct enumeration matches its stratum counts in five field/dimension settings. For n=4m,r=s=2m, substitution |GL_k|=q^{k²}φ_k yields q^{-4j²}φ_m^4/(φ_{m+j}²φ_{m-j}²). The bounded strictly positive Euler product φ∞ supplies a summable majorant, proving total-variation convergence. The scaled unconditioned probability has prefactor φ_{2m}^4/φ_{4m}→φ∞³ and sum→Θ/φ∞⁴, hence Θ/φ∞. The checker does not prove the infinite theorem or cover extension fields.

originality.rationale: The claim assessed for priority is the fixed-field balanced rank-half conditional discrete-theta law with a sharp commutativity-probability leading constant. The exact finite orbit formula and simultaneous diagonalization are classical inputs (Edmunds 2014), not asserted as original. Ferraz–Polcino Milies–Taufer (2017) counts individual idempotents/left ideals; Fulman–Guralnick (2016) counts unrestricted commuting matrices. The retrieved published records and targeted primary-source searches revealed no implication yielding this specific conditioned asymptotic without the present weighted-strata asymptotic argument. Risk remains for implicit coverage in broader module-count literature.

value.rationale: Ranks of commuting products of half-rank idempotents are intrinsic multiplication statistics in finite full matrix semigroups. A sharp q^{-n²/4} rarity law with nonzero Euler/theta constant and a nondegenerate fixed-field lattice fluctuation profile describes a natural balanced scaling regime. The result distinguishes counting single projections or unweighted conjugacy types from probabilistic behavior under an exponentially rare algebraic relation; its motivation and scope are substantive rather than arbitrary finite slicing.
